system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Splice the initial prompt containing the model role play definition, task goal, and tool definition with the input message to obtain the total prompt.
system_prompt_style.note: Each state has its own prompt with task target and IP variables rendered in.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: For each Agent state, we select relevant tools to provide the agent with relevant tasks to complete.
env_context_strategy.note: Agent explores with Terminal, browser and Search tools; no repo tree injected.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: each state only needs to understand the core task content and the output value of the previous state instead of obtaining all historical messages
context_compaction.note: State machine passes structured state-output between states rather than full history.

observation_format.evidence_quote: handles the natural language information exchanged between the agent calling tool and the target environment

tool_call_format.note: Model emits Action/Action Input parsed by a parsing function; commands executed in terminal.

tool_count.evidence_quote: Terminal is provided for Scanning status, Search is provided for Information Collection status, and Terminal and Playwright are provided for Exploiting status.
tool_count.note: Three tool types: Terminal, Playwright, Search, distributed across states.

edit_primitive.evidence_quote: Terminal is provided for Scanning status, Search is provided for Information Collection status, and Terminal and Playwright are provided for Exploiting status.
edit_primitive.note: No dedicated file-edit tool; edits only via terminal shell.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Tools description: Description of tools that the current agent and examples of tool input values can use.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: It uses the third-party architecture LangChain [10] to build an agent

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: we divide the PSM into the Agent state and the Rule state, constraining the workflow of solving tasks and guiding subsequent operations
loop_primitives.note: FSM over states (fixed transitions); within Agent states a ReAct think-act-observe loop.

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: For each Agent state, we prompt the model to generate thoughts and actions at each turn.
planning_granularity.note: No stored plan object; state machine drives flow, no explicit plan.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: divided the end-to-end penetration task into multiple states, and completed the entire task through state transition
multi_agent_topology.note: Each state runs an agent/rule; fixed sequence of specialised states.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: switches states after the task is completed, and reports its results to the next state without always maintaining the entire task context
delegation_mechanism.note: Control passes between states carrying output values.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: the entire process of completing automated penetration testing without human involvement

short_term_state.evidence_quote: the state carries information about the history of the machine and tracks how the state machine reached the current situation
short_term_state.note: FSM maintains structured state beyond messages.

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: we initialized the entire system for the next experiment
long_term_memory.note: System reinitialized between runs; no cross-run memory.

state_persistence.evidence_quote: initialized the entire system for the next experiment

self_verification.evidence_quote: In the check state, similar to the design in Section 3, we carefully set an output value for each vulnerability that can be obtained by successful exploitation according to the preset target information.
self_verification.note: Check state matches target string via rules, not model self-critique or tests run by harness on edits.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: the vulnerability exploitation status is returned within a certain threshold of vulnerability exploitation times. When the set number of vulnerability tests is exceeded, the current vulnerability is considered to be currently inexplicable, and the vulnerability is returned to the vulnerability selection stage
retry_policy.note: Retries vulnerabilities until success or all tried, capped by threshold.

rollback.evidence_quote: jumping back after checking the state will not have an impact on subsequent tests
rollback.note: State jumps but no filesystem/git revert of target changes described.

termination_condition.evidence_quote: repeated until the number of iteration steps reaches the preset maximum value or until the model actively exits the current state
termination_condition.note: Max iterations (set to 15), model exit, and Success/Failed final states on target-string match.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: limit the maximum iteration step to 15
cost_controls.note: Iteration cap only; no explicit token/cost budget mechanism described.

timeouts.evidence_quote: limit the maximum iteration step to 15
timeouts.note: No time-based timeout described, only iteration cap.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: We built a local Kali Linux Docker environment that installed all possible penetration tools for the model for the agent to perform operations, and gave it to the root user.

filesystem_access.evidence_quote: gave it to the root user. This ensures that the model has sufficient permissions to execute commands and ensures local security

network_policy.evidence_quote: The system interacts with target websites and Internet information through the external tools of these three modules.
network_policy.note: Search/browser access Internet; no egress restriction described.

permission_model.evidence_quote: gave it to the root user. This ensures that the model has sufficient permissions to execute commands
permission_model.note: Commands executed directly; no approval/allowlist described.

tracing.evidence_quote: we independently tested each vulnerability environment five times, recorded the results and necessary logs

replayability.evidence_quote: initialized the entire system for the next experiment

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: This includes all benchmark data, as well as the code used for pre-experiments and implementation of AutoPT.
eval_hooks.note: Benchmark with automated target-string checking shipped with AutoPT.

guardrails.evidence_quote: dangerous commands, such as “wget http://localhost -O- | sh” , may appear when the model is hallucinating
guardrails.note: Isolation used for safety; no explicit command-blocking filter described. Closest value; weak.

target_domain.evidence_quote: an automated penetration testing agent based on the principle of PSM driven by LLMs
target_domain.note: Web penetration testing domain; other in intent (security).

open_source.evidence_quote: To promote open science, we provided a Github 5 for future work.
open_source.note: Stated to be open-sourced after peer review; license not stated.

model_agnostic.evidence_quote: we built a pre-experimental environment through API requests
model_agnostic.note: Tested across GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, GPT-4o mini via API.

primary_artifact.note: No accessible pinned repo; coded from paper.
